diagnostic_evidence.quote: for all times $t \ge 0$, $\int_{\Omega} \mu(t,x) \, dx =1$ and $\mu(t,x)>0$ for all $x \in \Omega$

issues.failure_explanation: A variational solution lies in L^2(0,T;H^1) ∩ H^1(0,T;(H^1)^*), which embeds in C([0,T];L^2). So mu(0)=mu_0 must be in L^2, and no variational solution exists for mu_0 in L^1_+ \ L^2. Strict positivity for all t≥0 also fails at t=0 for data with zeros. The proof is only a pointer to external references with no check of these hypotheses.

failure_location.quote: Under the above assumptions on $V,W,\sigma$ and any $\mu_0\in L^1_+(\Omega)$, there exists a unique variational solution $\mu(t)$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Assume mu_0 in L^2_+ with unit mass (or enlarge the solution notion), and state strict positivity only for t>0.
issues.overall_effect: The stated scope (any L^1 probability density; positivity for all t≥0) is not supported. The later local-stabilization results use only small perturbations of a smooth equilibrium, so they are unaffected.
issues.title: Global well-posedness claimed for L^1 data and strict positivity at t=0, beyond the variational class
issues.why_classification: A hypothesis correction fixes the statement and leaves the rest of the paper's logic intact.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Namely, if $\nabla^2V(x)\succeq \alpha I$, and $\nabla^2 W(x)\succeq 0$ on $\T^d$, the free energy $\mathcal{F}[\mu]$ is displacement-convex,

issues.failure_explanation: The cited argument needs displacement convexity (Hess V ≥ alpha I, alpha>0). A periodic V on T^d cannot satisfy this, so that route is vacuous on the torus. The proposition's hypotheses are H-stability of W or smallness of ||W||_infty, which do not give displacement convexity. They need flat convexity or a Holley–Stroock-type LSI perturbation, which is not argued. The symbol beta is never defined (presumably 1/sigma).

failure_location.quote: which is rigorously proved in~\cite{malrieu2001logarithmic} for the Euclidean space $\R^d$ and is carried over the torus with periodic boundary conditions

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the justification by the correct torus argument (flat convexity of F for H-stable W; LSI by perturbation for small W), define beta=1/sigma, and drop the displacement-convexity remarks.
issues.overall_effect: Uniqueness of the stationary state and the exponential entropy/L^1 convergence are not supported by the stated justification, which does not match the hypotheses.
issues.title: Stationary-state uniqueness and convergence justified by displacement convexity, which cannot hold on the torus and is not the stated hypothesis
issues.why_classification: The results are plausible with a different, standard argument; this is a contained replacement of the proof route, not a loss of results.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: assuming that the initial condition has finite relative entropy with respect to $\bar\mu$

issues.failure_explanation: The right-hand side contains mu(.,.), which is meaningless; presumably mu_0 is meant. Even then, a pure L^1 contraction with prefactor 1 does not follow from LSI/entropy decay. Entropy methods with Csiszár–Kullback–Pinsker give a bound of the form sqrt(2 H(mu_0|mu_bar)) e^{-alpha t}. The hypothesis (finite relative entropy) does not match the stated bound. The alpha is also only said to be an appropriate constant.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the bound as ||mu(t)-mu_bar||_{L^1} <= sqrt(2 H(mu_0|mu_bar)) e^{-alpha t}, with alpha given by the LSI constant.
issues.overall_effect: The stated convergence inequality is not a valid consequence of the cited mechanism.
issues.title: Exponential convergence estimate is ill-formed and not implied by entropy decay
issues.why_classification: A one-line restatement via Pinsker's inequality restores a true statement of the same type; the result is not used later.

issues.failure_explanation: For V=0 and W=-K cos x the self-consistency relation gives mu_bar proportional to exp((K r/sigma) cos x). Linearizing r=Psi(Kr/sigma) with Psi'(0)=1/2 gives the critical coupling K_c=2 sigma. The remark writes exp(K r cos x), which is the sigma=1 case with K_c=2, but states K_c=1 for general sigma. K_c=1 holds only for sigma=1/2, as in the numerics, where the profile is exp(2Kr cos).

failure_location.quote: For $K\le1$ the uniform density $\mu\equiv(2\pi)^{-1}$ is the unique (and stable) equilibrium.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Write mu_bar proportional to exp(K r cos x / sigma) and the threshold K_c=2 sigma (equal to 1 only for sigma=1/2).
issues.overall_effect: The stated threshold and steady-state formula are wrong for the generic sigma of the remark.
issues.title: Kuramoto critical coupling and stationary profile inconsistent with the model's sigma
issues.why_classification: A local formula correction; nothing downstream depends on it.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We concludes the proof because $\Hcal$ is bounded from below given that it is the sum of a bounded operator $\Psi + \mathcal{K}$ with a bounded from below operator $-\Delta$.
Hence, for all $\mu \in \sigma(\Hcal)$, we have that $|\mu - \mu_n| \le \|\mathcal{K}\|$ for some $n \in \mathbb{N}$

issues.failure_explanation: H = H_loc + K with K a non-symmetric Hilbert–Schmidt operator, so H is not self-adjoint. The proof (Lemma perturb-pure plus K bounded) yields only a compact resolvent. Reality of the eigenvalues is not argued, and the paper's own later lemma only locates the spectrum in discs of radius ||K|| around real points. Biorthogonality and density of the generalized eigenfunctions of H and H* are never addressed; this is a nontrivial completeness question for a non-self-adjoint operator. Boundedness from below is not meaningful here and does not prove the claims.

failure_location.quote: Its spectrum consists of isolated real eigenvalues of finite multiplicity accumulating only at $\pm\infty$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either weaken the claim to a compact resolvent with discrete spectrum, or supply the extra argument (for example, self-adjointness of the linearized gradient-flow operator in the H^{-1}(mu_bar)-type inner product, plus a completeness theorem).
issues.overall_effect: The claimed spectral structure (real spectrum, biorthogonal complete eigenbasis) is unsupported. Later steps that treat eigenpairs of L and L* as real and biorthogonal rely on it.
issues.title: Pure-spectrum proposition asserts real eigenvalues and complete biorthogonal systems but proves only compact resolvent
issues.why_classification: Reality and completeness need a contained additional argument or a weakened statement. The main architecture survives because only finitely many unstable modes are used.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Since $\Pcal$ commutes with $\Lcal$ (mass conservation), it follows that $\Pcal_H$ commutes with $\Hcal$.

issues.failure_explanation: Zero total mass of the range gives L*mu_bar=0, i.e. mu_bar in ker L*, not ker L. In fact L mu_bar = A mu_bar + 2W(mu_bar) = W(mu_bar) = -sigma Δ mu_bar (for V=0) ≠0 for non-uniform mu_bar. So the proof's own statement mu_bar in ker(L) is false, and the next sentence contradicts it. Likewise P does not commute with L: mass conservation gives only P L = L, i.e. invariance of X_0, whereas L P = L - (∫·) L mu_bar ≠ P L. The conclusion 0 in sigma(L) and the reduction to X_0 survive because only range invariance is needed.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State that mu_bar lies in ker L* (so 0 is in sigma(L*) and hence in sigma(L)), and replace commutation by invariance of X_0 under L (P L = L).
issues.overall_effect: Two incorrect intermediate claims (ker L, commutation of P and H); the final conclusions can be rederived from range invariance.
issues.title: Mass conservation misused: kernel of L versus L*, and false commutation of P with L
issues.why_classification: A short local correction preserves all conclusions and the reduction to the zero-mean space.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: if and only if the right-hand side is orthogonal to the kernel of $\Hcal_{\mathrm{loc}}^\dagger = \Hcal_{\mathrm{loc}}$

issues.failure_explanation: For the self-adjoint H_loc, H_loc beta = f is solvable iff f is orthogonal to ker H_loc = span{sqrt(mu_bar)}, i.e. iff the integral of psi_j is 0. The proof instead requires only that phi_j is not a multiple of sqrt(mu_bar), which is neither equivalent nor sufficient (a vector outside the span need not be orthogonal to it). Remark kernel_L0 is cited for non-membership, which does not give the needed orthogonality. The orthogonality does hold for nonzero eigenvalues, since the range of L lies in the zero-mean space, but that argument is not given.

failure_location.quote: the equation is solvable if and only if $\varphi_j \notin \operatorname{span}\{ \sqrt{\bar\mu} \}$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the criterion by orthogonality: show psi_j has zero mean (psi_j lies in X_0 for lambda_j≠0), so phi_j is orthogonal to sqrt(mu_bar) and the equation is solvable.
issues.overall_effect: Existence of the shape functions alpha_j, hence the construction of B and the stabilizability claim, is justified by an invalid criterion.
issues.title: Solvability of the shape-function equation: Fredholm alternative misapplied (orthogonality replaced by non-membership in the kernel span)
issues.why_classification: The correct condition is true by the zero-mean property and the fix is a short local substitution that preserves the theorem.

issues.failure_explanation: Lemma spectrum_finite gives finitely many distinct eigenvalues with Re ≥ -delta, not m eigenpairs counted with multiplicity. The proof silently treats each eigenvalue as having a single eigenvector and normalizes <psi_j,phi_i>=delta_ij. The Hautus test needs B* injective on the whole eigenspace ker(lambda-L*) for every unstable lambda. If an eigenvalue has geometric multiplicity >1 (e.g. cos kx, sin kx modes), one shape function per eigenvalue is insufficient. If it has a nontrivial Jordan chain, <psi,phi>=0 for all eigenvectors, so the normalization is impossible and B* can vanish on an eigenvector. Neither case is excluded or treated. The statement also says only 'the first m eigenpairs' satisfy the real-part condition, which does not say all unstable modes are covered.

failure_location.quote: Let $(\lambda_i, \phi_i)$ for $i=1,\dots,m$ be the eigenpairs of $\Lcal^*$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the theorem with m equal to the total (algebraic) multiplicity of the spectrum in Re ≥ -delta, choose psi_j as a basis of the (generalized) eigenspace, prove semisimplicity or treat Jordan chains, and verify injectivity of B* on every eigenspace of L*.
issues.overall_effect: The claim that (L,B) satisfies the infinite-dimensional Hautus test and is delta-stabilizable is not established in general (multiple or non-semisimple unstable eigenvalues).
issues.title: Hautus verification assumes one eigenvector per eigenvalue and a biorthogonal normalization, and checks only chosen eigenvectors
issues.why_classification: A contained additional argument on multiplicities (a semisimplicity lemma or generalized eigenvectors) fixes it, without changing the overall design.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: generates an exponentially stable semigroup on $\Space_0$

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem claims a bound on (0,∞) with a constant independent of time. A sectorial operator plus a bounded perturbation has maximal L^2 regularity only on finite intervals, or on the half-line with exponential stability. The proof never invokes the exponential stability supplied by the Riccati feedback (Prop ARE), which is what makes the (0,∞) estimate possible. The decomposition is also inconsistent: A is defined as lambda I - H_loc, B has the opposite sign for K, and A+B does not equal H_Pi. Sectoriality of H_loc is attributed to Prop pure-spectrum, which concerns H.

failure_location.quote: so that the operator $A+B$ meets the hypotheses of the maximal-$L^2$-regularity theorem

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Write H_Pi = H_loc + bounded, note it generates an analytic semigroup that is exponentially stable by Prop ARE, and deduce maximal L^2 regularity on (0,∞) from the finite-horizon result plus exponential stability.
issues.overall_effect: The global-in-time estimate used for the contraction argument and local decay rests on an incomplete proof.
issues.title: Infinite-horizon maximal regularity asserted without using exponential stability of the closed-loop semigroup
issues.why_classification: The missing ingredient is already established in the paper (Prop ARE), and a standard short argument supplies the half-line estimate with no change to the statement.
